cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: The practical component is worth 60% of the total GCSE — performance and choreography combined

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Performance (30%) includes one solo and one duet/trio performance of set phrases

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Choreography (30%) requires a solo or group choreography in response to a chosen stimulus

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Performance marks reward technical accuracy, physical skills, expressive skills and mental skills

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Technical accuracy includes alignment, coordination, control, balance and spatial awareness

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Expressive skills include projection, focus, musicality, communication of choreographic intent

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Mental skills include commitment, concentration, confidence and responsiveness to feedback

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Choreography marks reward creative response, choreographic intention, structure and use of devices

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Keep a choreographic diary — it provides evidence of your process and supports the written programme note

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Rehearse under exam conditions to build confidence and reduce nerves on the day

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: Video yourself in rehearsal to identify areas for improvement that you may not feel from inside the movement

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Exam Technique
cards.back: The programme note is assessed alongside your choreography — write it clearly, linking intention to movement

cards.front: What should you know about gcse dance exam tips — practical exam technique?
cards.back: 1. For Practical Exam Technique questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Practical Exam Technique 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
Explain how preparation and rehearsal strategies can maximise your marks in the AQA 8236 practical components. [6 marks]

AO1 (Performance): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of practical exam technique, including choreographic processes, performing skills and dance appreciation relevant to AQA 8236. AO2 (Choreography): Apply knowledge and understanding of practical exam technique through the creative process of choreography, selecting and using movement material and choreographic devices. AO3 (Appreciation): A
